value_chain_position: Fuel systems, combustion and actuation controls for aerospace engines and industrial gas turbines. The industrial-turbine controls slice sells into power-generation original-equipment makers such as GE Vernova, Baker Hughes and Mitsubishi, plus high-speed diesel fuel injection into Rolls-Royce mtu backup-power engines for data centres. Aerospace, about 61% of revenue, sits outside this book's chain.
cost_curve_verified: Woodward has no output commodity and therefore no unit cost curve; the equivalent lie-detector is price realisation against gross margin, and here the deterministic proxy DISAGREES with the company because it is stale, not wrong: our scan carries gross margin at 26.8% and net debt at $395M (both fiscal-2025 annual), whereas the 30 June 2026 filing shows gross margin of 31.5% in the quarter (29.5% trailing twelve months) and net debt of $885M including $18M of capitalised leases; separately our leverage proxy of 0.86x earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation is a net-debt measure while management reported 1.6x on 2026-07-29 using gross debt, a definitional gap rather than a discrepancy - the sum-of-the-parts below subtracts the $885M lease-inclusive net debt figure.
gm_trajectory: Expanding, and expanding hard: gross margin rose to 31.5% in the June-2026 quarter from 27.2% a year earlier (+430 basis points) while revenue grew 21.2% to $1,109.7M, and the trailing-twelve-month rate is 29.5% versus 26.8% for fiscal 2025 - expanding margin on strongly growing revenue is genuine pricing power in a supply-constrained niche, not commoditisation bought with volume; the qualification management itself supplied on 2026-07-29 is that company-wide price realisation was 10% in the quarter and about 8% for fiscal 2026 but is guided to 3-5% thereafter, and about 100 basis points of the Aerospace margin came from a one-time retroactive contract price true-up.
bull_thesis: Woodward is a certified, sole-source supplier of flight-critical and turbine-critical hardware sitting in front of two demand waves at once, and it has just proved it can convert that position into price. The June-2026 quarter, reported 2026-07-29, showed revenue up 21.2% to $1,109.7M with gross margin up 430 basis points to 31.5%, Aerospace margin at 24.0% against 21.1%, and core Industrial margin at 21.2% against 15.6%. Adjusted earnings per share rose 43% to $2.52 and management raised full-year guidance for the third time in one fiscal year, to $9.30-$9.50, with Aerospace revenue up 21-23% at roughly 23.5% margins and Industrial up 19-21% at roughly 19%. The first engine is the aircraft maintenance cycle. Service content on CFM LEAP and Pratt geared-turbofan units runs roughly five times the legacy generation, the installed base is compounding hours and cycles, and management confirmed on 2026-07-29 that monthly shop inputs across V2500, CFM56, GEnx and GE90 units show no downtrend. Woodward is expanding that franchise without spending its own capital: the HAECO Elite Licensed Repair Service Facility agreement announced 2026-07-21 is the third such licence, and it lets Woodward supply the materials, work scopes and technical approach while a partner funds the shop. Content per aircraft is also rising: the A350 wing spoiler award plus the acquired Safran horizontal stabiliser trim actuator line take A350 shipset value to about $550,000 once spoiler deliveries begin in late calendar 2028, and the Valve Research solenoid purchase closed in March 2026 positions the company for the next single-aisle competition. The second engine is power. Industrial revenue grew 26% in the June quarter, with power generation up 19% on data-centre base and backup demand and oil and gas up 11% on liquefied-natural-gas infrastructure. The expanded Glatten, Germany high-speed fuel-injection plant was inaugurated 2026-07-21, on schedule and on budget, and is already shipping into Rolls-Royce mtu power-generation demand. The decisive datapoint is the order signal behind it: on 2026-07-29 the chief executive said that for several quarters running, numerous customers have raised their forecasts for 2027, 2028 and into the early 2030s, and that if those cases hold Woodward will have to expand capacity beyond what it has already built. Underneath both engines is a self-help story that is landing on time. Every dated promise across eight quarterly calls has been kept - Glatten complete, Spartanburg on schedule for 2027, the China on-highway wind-down finishing this fiscal year at the guided $20-25M restructuring cost, the acquired Canadian electronics plant being consolidated into Poland and Bulgaria. Automation is now quantified rather than aspirational: roughly 1,000 fewer incremental hires by 2029, about half of projected hiring needs. Return on invested capital has climbed to about 11.9% trailing from roughly 7.8% on the fiscal-2025 annual basis, and return on equity to 21.7%. The balance sheet supports all of it at 1.6 times gross debt to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. Conditions that must hold: aftermarket shop inputs must not roll over as legacy fleets retire and release used serviceable material; the data-centre power forecasts must convert from customer forecasts into firm orders; and productivity plus volume leverage must replace the price lever as it fades to 3-5%. If all three hold, fiscal 2027 delivers high-single to low-double-digit revenue growth on 30-35% incremental margins, the March 2027 Investor Day resets the Industrial margin target above the current mid-teens framework, and the shares can carry an aerospace-aftermarket multiple.
bear_thesis: The bear case is not that Woodward is a bad business - it is that the market is paying a peak multiple for peak inputs that management has itself told investors are ending. Start with what is actually producing the earnings. On 2026-07-29 the chief executive attributed the margin expansion to pricing, and the chief financial officer put company-wide price realisation at 10% in the June quarter and about 8% for fiscal 2026, then said plainly that the first post-2022 round of long-term agreements is now closed out and that 3-5% is the normal forward rate. Of roughly 21 percentage points of current revenue growth, about 8 points is a lever with a stated expiry date. Three further supports come out of the model in fiscal 2027 at the same time. The China on-highway line, worth about $130M of fiscal-2026 revenue and about 90 basis points of Industrial segment margin in the June quarter alone, goes to zero. The one-time retroactive contract price true-up worth about 100 basis points of Aerospace margin does not repeat. And the June-quarter core Industrial margin of 21.2% was flattered by business mix, which the chief financial officer immediately guided back to first-half levels of roughly 17-18%. Strip those out and the underlying trajectory is far flatter than the headline. Now the cash. Management raised earnings guidance three times in fiscal 2026 and never raised free-cash-flow guidance, because the inventory-turn improvement in the original plan was abandoned to protect deliveries. Trailing free cash flow of $377M converts only 68% of $552M of trailing net income; receivables of $1,056M represent 92 days of sales; capital spending is guided to $290M for the fiscal year against $156M spent in nine months, so the fourth quarter alone must nearly match the first three combined. On top of that sits an undefined, deferred capacity expansion for data-centre power that management has now pushed twice, most recently to the March 2027 Investor Day. Growth capital spending is going up, not down, into a demand signal that is a forecast rather than a backlog. Capital discipline is the weakest link, and nobody on eight consecutive calls asked about it. Over the last four reported quarters Woodward spent $602M repurchasing stock - about 2.7% of its market value - while the diluted share count fell 0.09% and the basic count actually rose 0.3%. That is not a return of capital; it is the funding of employee share compensation, executed at 40 times earnings while the stock ran to a 52-week high of $450.92. It was funded with debt: net debt went from roughly $391M at the September-2025 year end to $885M at 30 June 2026. Insiders sold 47,254 shares across 62 open-market disposals over the window with zero open-market purchases. Commodities are input costs here, not revenue. On 2026-07-29 the chief executive named castings, forgings and specifically rare earth metals as the constraint the whole industry forecasts becoming a big challenge within the next few quarters, and Woodward is already machining parts from billet rather than castings - a deliberately wasteful use of material chosen for supply continuity. Every dollar of copper, nickel, rare-earth and forging inflation lands in cost of goods sold at the exact moment the price lever falls from 10% to 3-5%. Woodward carries 5-10 problematic suppliers at any time and runs three rapid-response machining centres to bail them out; that is a permanent cost the productivity story has to overcome before it produces any expansion. The order-cancellation path is concrete. In Aerospace, the chief executive warned in July 2025 that once legacy aircraft are parked, used serviceable material floods the aftermarket and could eat into the business quickly - and legacy overhaul demand running hotter than modelled for two straight years makes that reversal larger, not smaller. Commercial original-equipment growth of 34% is a build-rate pass-through; if Boeing or Airbus stall a rate break, Woodward destocks, exactly as it did in fiscal 2025. In Industrial, the power-generation order book is a set of customer forecasts for 2027 through the early 2030s with no disclosed backlog, no book-to-bill figure, no named counterparty beyond Rolls-Royce mtu, and no signed power-purchase agreements or interconnection positions - Woodward is three steps removed from the data centre and takes the cancellation before the turbine maker does. Price the damage. If fiscal 2027 sees Aerospace revenue up only 5% with margin back to 21% as the retroactive price and spare-unit provisioning normalise, and Industrial revenue falls to about $1.38B on the China exit plus a data-centre order pause at a 15.5% margin, segment earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation fall to roughly $700M and $266M respectively. Apply mid-cycle multiples of 18 and 12 times against corporate costs at 16 times, subtract about $1.0B of net debt after another year of elevated capital spending and buybacks, and the equity is worth about $195 per share - roughly half today's price and below the 52-week low of $233.31, because in that scenario earnings and the multiple fall together. What would confirm it: fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 price realisation printing below 6%, spare line-replaceable-unit orders normalising toward first-half levels as guided, a fiscal-2027 guide with incremental margins below 30%, or an Investor Day capacity announcement that commits capital against forecasts rather than firm orders.
sop_bull: Favourable sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately), on fiscal-2027 estimated segment earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, per share in US dollars: Aerospace $860M of segment earnings (revenue about $3.16B, up 12%, at a roughly 27% margin as productivity and automation replace price) valued at 28 times, in line with the certified-aftermarket comparables Heico at 39 times and Curtiss-Wright at 35 times, gives $24,080M. Industrial $375M (revenue about $1.60B after absorbing the China on-highway exit, at a roughly 23% margin) valued at 22 times on a data-centre power re-rating toward Eaton at 32 times and GE Aerospace at 33 times, gives $8,250M. Unallocated corporate costs of $170M capitalised at 25 times deduct $4,250M. Enterprise value $28,080M, less net debt of $885M as at 30 June 2026, gives equity of $27,195M; over about 60.3M diluted shares that is roughly $451 per share. This case requires the March 2027 Investor Day to reset Industrial margin targets upward and to convert the customer power-generation forecasts into a funded, contracted capacity expansion, and it requires the aftermarket to keep compounding as the LEAP and geared-turbofan installed base crosses over legacy repair revenue in late calendar 2026 or early 2027.
sop_bear: Adverse sum-of-the-parts, assuming the power-for-artificial-intelligence chain turns against Woodward - data-centre forecasts are deferred rather than ordered, input costs rise, and price reverts - on fiscal-2027 estimates: Aerospace revenue about $2.96B (up only 5% as airframer rate breaks slip and spare line-replaceable-unit provisioning normalises) at a 21% segment operating margin gives $622M of operating profit, plus about $78M of depreciation and amortisation, for $700M of segment earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; valued at 18 times, a mid-cycle component-supplier multiple rather than the current aftermarket premium, that is $12,600M. Industrial revenue falls to about $1.38B - the roughly $130M China on-highway line is gone and core growth stalls as customers pause orders - at a 15.5% operating margin, giving $214M plus about $52M of depreciation and amortisation, or $266M; valued at 12 times, that is $3,192M. Unallocated corporate costs of $170M at 16 times deduct $2,720M. Enterprise value $13,072M, less about $1.0B of net debt after another year of $290M-plus capital spending and continued buybacks, gives equity of about $12,072M; over about 61.5M diluted shares that is roughly $195 per share. The mechanism is that earnings and the multiple compress together: the same rare-earth, casting and forging inflation the chief executive flagged on 2026-07-29 lands in cost of goods sold precisely as price realisation falls from 10% to the guided 3-5%, so a 6-point gross-margin give-back accompanies a de-rating from 27.6 times trailing enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation toward the high teens.
sop_breakdown: Base-case sum-of-the-parts on fiscal-2027 estimated segment earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, splitting the difference between the favourable and adverse multiple sets because the aerospace and electrical comparable group is itself at a multi-year multiple high: Aerospace $830M of segment earnings (revenue about $3.10B, up 10%, margin roughly 26.8%) at 24 times = $19,920M, a discount to Heico at 39 times and Curtiss-Wright at 35 times that reflects Woodward's lower 11.9% return on invested capital and its position one rung below the engine makers who own the platform specification. Industrial $350M (revenue about $1.56B after the roughly $130M China on-highway exit, margin roughly 22.4%) at 17 times = $5,950M, between Parker Hannifin at 24 times and a mid-cycle components multiple, because the data-centre power demand is disclosed as customer forecasts rather than backlog. Unallocated corporate costs of $170M capitalised at 21 times = minus $3,570M. Enterprise value $22,300M, less net debt of $885M at 30 June 2026 (including $18M of capitalised leases; the ex-lease figure management would quote is $867M), gives equity of $21,415M. Over about 61.0M diluted shares that is $351 per share. Cross-check: this equals about 22 times fiscal-2027 estimated consolidated earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of roughly $1,010M and about 33 times fiscal-2027 estimated earnings per share of roughly $10.45 - a full multiple for a high-single-digit grower, and still 7% below where the stock trades.
risk_reward: Levels only, in US dollars per share against a market price of $375.89 on 2026-08-04: the adverse case breaks at $195, the base-case sum-of-the-parts fair value is $351, and the favourable case reaches $451. The stock therefore trades above its base-case fair value, with roughly 2.5 times as much distance to the adverse case as to the favourable one. There is no structural floor: net debt of $885M means there is no net cash per share to fall back on, there is no deal, tender or announced asset sale, and the 52-week low of $233.31 is a chart level rather than a floor.
catalyst_status_note: The load-bearing event is the data-centre power-generation capacity decision - how much capital Woodward will commit against customer forecasts for 2027, 2028 and into the early 2030s. It is non-binding and has now been deferred twice: on the 2026-04-29 call the chief executive said multiple customers had shared potential increases to their forecasts and that Woodward was evaluating options; on the 2026-07-29 call he again declined to size it, saying the company is in detailed discussions about the risk case and will be in a better position to talk about what that looks like at its Investor Day. That Investor Day was given a firm date on the same call: Thursday 4 March 2027, in New York City. So the date is fixed but the payout is not contractual and the decision itself has slipped a quarter already. Verified operating events that have already happened and are therefore spent, not pending: the expanded Glatten, Germany high-speed fuel-injection plant was inaugurated 2026-07-21 (company release, and described on the 2026-07-29 call as on schedule and on budget); the HAECO Elite Licensed Repair Service Facility agreement for CFM LEAP-1A, -1B and -1C components was announced 2026-07-21 (company release); third-quarter fiscal-2026 results and the third guidance raise of the year landed 2026-07-29. Per this lane's rules the status is descriptive only and does not move the verdict.
peer_comps_note: Measured on enterprise value to trailing twelve-month earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation from Financial Modeling Prep as at 2026-08-04, Woodward sits at 27.6 times, which is squarely at - not below - the blended value of its assigned competitor set weighted 61% aerospace and 39% industrial. The certified-aftermarket names trade higher: Heico at 39.4 times and Curtiss-Wright at 35.5 times, both with returns on invested capital comparable to or better than Woodward's 11.9% (Curtiss-Wright 12.7%, Heico 10.9%). The electrical and power comparables straddle it: Eaton at 31.9 times, GE Aerospace at 33.0 times, Parker Hannifin at 24.0 times. Two set members are not clean reads and are weighted lightly: TransDigm prints 14.3 times, but it carries 4.3 times net leverage and negative book equity, so its enterprise-value multiple is not comparable to an unlevered component maker; and Honeywell prints 7.9 times on a market capitalisation of only $79B, which reflects a post-separation stub rather than the diversified aerospace comparable it once was. Moog class A returned no data from the provider. The conclusion is uncomfortable for the bull: at 61% aerospace weighted at roughly 30 times and 39% industrial weighted at roughly 22 times, the peer-implied blended multiple is about 27 times - essentially where Woodward already trades. There is no relative-value discount here to harvest; the base case above deliberately marks the parts below the live comparable set because that comparable set is itself at a multi-year multiple high.
consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is not about the quality of the business - it is about which of Woodward's fiscal-2026 earnings drivers survive into fiscal 2027, and the disagreement is with the street's arithmetic rather than its enthusiasm. The street is anchored high and clustered: consensus target $442.50, median $440.00, high $470.00, low $420.00, and every single published target sits above the current $375.89. The freshest marks are Truist at $420.00 dated 2026-08-04 and RBC at $430.00 dated 2026-07-30, both set after the third-quarter print, and the average target has climbed from $388.11 over the past year to $425.00 over the past month. Consensus forward earnings growth is +13.5%. The specific street assumption we believe is wrong is that fiscal-2026 momentum extrapolates. Management said the opposite on its own call on 2026-07-29. The chief financial officer put company-wide price realisation at 10% in the June quarter and about 8% for the fiscal year, then said the first post-2022 round of long-term agreements is closed out and that 3-5% is the normal forward rate. That is not our inference; it is guidance. Roughly 8 of the 21 percentage points of current revenue growth has a stated expiry. Three more supports vanish at the same moment. The China on-highway product line - about $130M of fiscal-2026 revenue, and worth about 90 basis points of Industrial segment margin in the June quarter because it flowed through above breakeven - goes to zero in fiscal 2027 by management's own decision. The retroactive contract price true-up that added roughly 100 basis points to Aerospace margin was explicitly one-time. And the eye-catching 21.2% core Industrial margin was walked back inside the same call: the chief financial officer said business-unit mix played favourably and that he expects core Industrial earnings back at first-half levels of roughly 17-18% next quarter. A model that carries 21% Industrial margins forward is carrying a mix quarter forward. The second thing the street is under-weighting is cash. Woodward raised earnings guidance three times this fiscal year and never once raised free-cash-flow guidance. Pressed on exactly this by Wells Fargo on 2026-07-29, the chief financial officer explained that the inventory-turn improvement built into the original plan was deliberately abandoned to protect deliveries. The result is that trailing free cash flow of $377M converts only 68% of $552M of trailing net income, receivables run at 92 days of sales, and capital spending is guided to $290M against $156M spent in nine months. On a $22.4B market capitalisation that is a free-cash-flow yield of about 1.7%. The street is valuing an earnings stream that is not turning into cash at anything like the same rate, and growth capital spending is about to step up again for a data-centre capacity expansion that has not been sized. Third, and least discussed: nobody on eight consecutive earnings calls asked why $602M of share repurchases over the last four quarters - about 2.7% of the market value - produced a 0.09% reduction in diluted shares and a 0.3% increase in basic shares. Funded with debt, at 40 times earnings, while the stock ran to a 52-week high of $450.92. That is share-compensation funding presented as capital return, and it is a live item for the March 2027 Investor Day. Where the street is right and we will not argue: aftermarket demand is genuinely holding. Management tracks monthly shop inputs by unit type - V2500 fuel controls, CFM56 hydro-mechanical units, GEnx, GE90 - and reported on 2026-07-29 that there is no downtrend, only normal noise. We accept that. Our disagreement is about price, not volume.
valley_of_death: The risky window is the next three to nine months, and it is unusually well-signposted because management supplied most of the signposts itself. The first pressure point is the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, ending 30 September 2026 and reported in late November. Three separate things compress it. Capital spending must nearly double sequentially: $290M is guided for the year against $156M spent in nine months, with the chief financial officer confirming the fourth-quarter concentration is chunky - finishing the Spartanburg facility and purchasing A350 spoiler production machinery. That is roughly $134M of capital spending against a quarter that generated $87M of free cash flow in the third quarter. The second is that spare line-replaceable-unit orders, which have been running hot for several quarters, were explicitly guided down: elevated but coming down slightly from the third quarter, back toward first-half levels. The third is that China on-highway revenue, worth $40M and about 90 basis points of Industrial margin in the June quarter, goes to essentially nothing in the fourth quarter as the wind-down completes. A guidance range of $9.30-$9.50 with nine months of $6.76 reported leaves no cushion for all three to land at once. The second pressure point is the fiscal-2027 guide, delivered with fourth-quarter results in November 2026. This is where the price cliff becomes a printed number. Going from about 8% price realisation to the guided 3-5% removes roughly 4 to 5 percentage points of revenue growth before any volume assumption, and the China exit removes about 3 more. A high-single-digit revenue guide with incremental margins at or below the 30-35% long-term framework is the likely shape, and against a stock at 40 times trailing earnings that is a de-rating event even if the business is performing exactly as management intends. Note that the chief executive twice declined to pre-commit to fiscal-2027 incremental margins on the 2026-07-29 call, saying it is premature and that is the guidance for next year. The third pressure point is input costs, and it is the one management has flagged but not sized. Commodities are a cost here, not a revenue: rising copper, nickel, forging and rare-earth prices land in cost of goods sold for an equipment maker. On 2026-07-29 the chief executive named castings, forgings and rare earth metals as the constraint the whole industry forecasts becoming a big challenge within the next few quarters, and said Woodward has been machining parts from solid billet instead - explicitly not a very efficient use of material, chosen for supply continuity. Woodward is also carrying 5-10 problematic suppliers at any time and running three rapid-response machining centres to bail them out. If rare-earth availability tightens in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026 as management expects, the cost hits in the same quarters that price realisation falls to 3-5%. Fourth, the balance sheet has less slack than it did. Net debt went from roughly $391M at the September-2025 year end to $885M at 30 June 2026, and gross leverage is 1.6 times earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. Woodward is still comfortable, but it is simultaneously committed to about $700M of shareholder returns this fiscal year, $290M of capital spending, and an unsized data-centre capacity expansion. Something gives, and the buyback is the flexible item. What is not in this window: there is no debt maturity wall, no cash burn, and no covenant risk. Trailing operating cash flow of $585M comfortably covers everything. This is a valuation and expectations risk, not a solvency risk.
positioning_washout: There is no mechanical forced-selling dynamic here, and investors waiting for one will wait a long time. Woodward pays a small dividend - about $55M over nine months against $553M of buybacks - so the shareholder base is not yield-driven and there is no dividend cut to trigger income-fund liquidation. There is no pivot, no strategic review, no index reclassification pending, and no leverage stress that would force a de-risking. Liquidity is ample at roughly $119M of average daily dollar volume against a $22.4B market capitalisation, so even a large institutional exit clears without dislocation. What exists instead is a softer, slower version of the same thing: momentum unwinding. The shares trade at $375.89 against a 50-day average of $392.91 and a 52-week high of $450.92 - about 17% below the high - and yet they are still 8% above the 200-day average of $348.17 and sit 60% of the way up the 52-week range. The stock sold off into a beat-and-raise, which is the classic signature of a name where the marginal buyer is a growth or momentum holder rather than a valuation buyer. Our positioning inputs show a smart-money score of 64 out of 100 with institutional flow neutral at 50 out of 100 - engaged but not crowded, which cuts both ways: there is no capitulation set-up to buy, and no obvious ballast either. The one genuinely one-sided signal is insider behaviour. Over the observed window there were zero open-market purchases against 62 open-market disposals covering 47,254 shares. Management is a consistent seller into strength and, through the buyback, the company is the offsetting buyer of those same shares. That is not forced selling, but it does tell you who is on which side at these prices. The realistic path to a genuine wash-out is not mechanical - it is a fiscal-2027 guide in November 2026 that prints high-single-digit revenue growth and sub-30% incremental margins, causing the growth-at-a-reasonable-price holders to reprice the multiple rather than the earnings. That would be an ordinary de-rating, not a liquidation, and it is the level at which this becomes an interesting purchase.
forcing_function: Three dated events, in the order they arrive. First and most important, the fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results, due in late November 2026 based on the company's consistent pattern (fiscal 2025 results were reported 2025-11-24). This is not primarily about the fourth quarter; it is the call at which Woodward must guide fiscal 2027 and therefore must put a number on the price cliff. Management has told the market that price realisation goes from about 8% to 3-5%, that the roughly $130M China on-highway line is gone, and that a one-time retroactive contract price true-up worth about 100 basis points of Aerospace margin does not repeat. All three land in one guide. The chief executive twice declined on 2026-07-29 to pre-commit to fiscal-2027 incremental margins, calling it premature. Whichever way that guide prints, it resolves the central disagreement in this file. Second, the Investor Day, given a firm date on the 2026-07-29 call: Thursday 4 March 2027, in New York City. This is where the data-centre power capacity decision - deferred from the April 2026 call to the July 2026 call and then to this date - finally gets sized, and where the Industrial margin target is reset from the mid-teens framework set at the December 2023 Investor Day against 21.2% core delivered in the June quarter. It is a firm, scheduled corporate event but a non-binding one: no contract, no payout, no third-party commitment. A credible, contracted capacity expansion announced there is the single most plausible mechanism for a re-rating of the industrial half of the business toward the power-for-artificial-intelligence multiples that Eaton at 31.9 times and GE Aerospace at 33.0 times currently command. An expansion committed against customer forecasts rather than firm orders would be the opposite. Third, the intervening quarterly prints - first quarter fiscal 2027 in early February 2027 - which will show whether spare line-replaceable-unit orders normalised as guided and whether the rare-earth and casting constraints the chief executive flagged for the next few quarters actually bit. What would force a re-rating upward before any of these: a named, dated, funded power-generation capacity contract with a disclosed customer and volume. Woodward has never disclosed a backlog figure or a book-to-bill ratio on any of these eight calls, and the absence is itself the point - the power-for-artificial-intelligence demand is described as customer forecasts for 2027 through the early 2030s, which is not an order book.
moderator_conclusion: This is an excellent business at a price that already reflects it, and the honest call is to wait rather than to pass. Take the operating verification first, because it is genuinely strong. Gross margin rose to 31.5% in the June-2026 quarter from 27.2% a year earlier while revenue grew 21.2% - expanding margin on strongly growing revenue is the clean signature of pricing power in a supply-constrained niche, and it is the opposite of commoditisation bought with volume. Every dated operational promise across eight quarterly calls has landed: the Glatten, Germany fuel-injection expansion was inaugurated 2026-07-21 on schedule and on budget, Spartanburg is on track for 2027, the China on-highway wind-down is finishing at the guided cost, and the acquired actuation businesses are being integrated with named plant consolidations. Guidance was raised three times in one fiscal year with no offsetting cut and seven earnings beats in seven quarters. Return on invested capital is rising toward 11.9%, return on equity is 21.7%, and gross leverage is a comfortable 1.6 times. The forensic file supports a credibility score of 4 and a strengthening trajectory. The moat is narrow but genuinely widening: certified, sole-source flight-critical hardware protected by the same certification that protects its aftermarket, with content per aircraft rising - A350 shipset value going to about $550,000 - and service content on new-generation engines running roughly five times the legacy generation. The structural risks that would impair terminal value are manageable rather than terminal; sustainable fuels, hybrid propulsion and grid decarbonisation all still need fuel metering, combustion control and actuation, and several increase Woodward content. Now the three lane tests. On pricing power, Woodward passes clearly, with the qualification that management itself has dated the expiry: price realisation of 10% in the quarter and about 8% for the year, guided to 3-5% thereafter because the first post-2022 round of long-term agreements is closed out. On order-book durability, Woodward fails the disclosure test outright. There is no backlog figure, no book-to-bill ratio, and no named counterparty or contracted volume anywhere in eight calls. The data-centre power demand that gives this name its place in this book is described as customer forecasts for 2027, 2028 and into the early 2030s - forecasts, not orders, and Woodward sits three steps removed from the data centre, behind the engine maker, behind the turbine maker. Undated backlog language is worth nothing, and Woodward has not even given us undated backlog language. On capital discipline, the record is mixed and worse than the operating record. Capital spending is well-directed and management is refusing to over-commit to the power expansion, which is admirable at this point in a capital cycle. But over the last four quarters Woodward spent $602M on repurchases - about 2.7% of its market value - and the diluted share count fell 0.09% while the basic count rose 0.3%. That is share-compensation funding presented as capital return, executed at 40 times earnings while the stock ran to a 52-week high of $450.92, and funded with debt: net debt went from about $391M to $885M in nine months. Insiders sold 47,254 shares across 62 disposals with zero open-market purchases. On the regime, the assigned power-for-artificial-intelligence chain reads neutral, and commodities are input costs here, not revenue - rising copper, nickel, forging and rare-earth prices are a margin headwind for an equipment maker. The chief executive named rare earth metals on 2026-07-29 as an industry-wide constraint expected to become a big challenge within the next few quarters, and Woodward is already machining from billet instead of castings at a deliberate material-cost penalty. That cost arrives in the same quarters the price lever falls. Reconciling the two sum-of-the-parts builds gives a base-case fair value of $351 per share, against $451 in the favourable case and $195 in the adverse case, with the stock at $375.89. The base case marks the parts below the live comparable set on purpose: at 61% aerospace and 39% industrial, the peer-implied blended multiple is about 27 times enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, which is exactly where Woodward already trades at 27.6 times - so there is no relative-value discount to harvest, and the comparable set itself is at a multi-year high. There is no structural floor; net debt of $885M means no net cash to fall back on, and the 52-week low of $233.31 is a chart level, not a floor. The timing call is therefore to wait for the wash-out rather than to buy now, and the specific level is below $300 - roughly 20 times fiscal-2027 estimated consolidated earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, and about a 15% margin of safety to the base case. The specific development that would produce it is the fiscal-2027 guide at the fourth-quarter results in late November 2026, when the price cliff, the China on-highway exit and the non-repeating retroactive price true-up all land in one number. If that guide prints high-single-digit revenue growth with incremental margins at or below the long-term 30-35% framework, a 40-times multiple does not survive contact with it, and Woodward becomes a name worth owning at a price where the aftermarket compounding and the data-centre content are not already fully paid for. The two scores diverge deliberately. The execution score of 3 reflects a real, strengthening franchise whose entry price is wrong today but whose thesis is intact and whose trigger is dated. The value score of 2 reflects that on valuation and forensic quality alone - ignoring any event overlay and any regime tilt - the stock trades 7% above base-case fair value at a 1.7% free-cash-flow yield, with the largest earnings driver publicly scheduled to fade and a buyback that returns no ownership to shareholders. Good company, wrong price, and the date on which the price gets tested is already on the calendar.
